newsitem.title: USA: United Airlines to launch new ads - NYT.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines to launch new ads - NYT.

text.p: Move over "Fly the Friendly Skies." Here comes "A better way for cynics to travel" or "Wouldn't it be great if we could all fly commercials?"

The New York Times in its Friday edition said that United Airlines plans to launch a new advertising campaign next Thursday that seeks to empathize with some of the hassles of flying. The campaign is in sharp contrast to traditional airline advertisements that accentuate the positive with a near-sense of euphoria.
Instead, United is looking to acknowledge just how problematic the skies, the gates, the planes and even its employees can be for travelers, especially frequent fliers, the Times said.

"'Friendly skies' was created at a time when a lot of people were afraid to fly and when friendliness was of higher value," said Bill Westbrook, president and chief executive of ad agency Fallon McElligott. "It's a wonderful part of advertising history, but the market changed."
United spokesman John Kiker said the new campaign was based on interviews with consumers.
"They said, 'Don't lie to us anymore,'" Kiker said.
